idiom_name: Prettier plus typescript-eslint depth and exhaustiveness rules
implementation_notes: TypeScript inherits JavaScript's tooling: Prettier owns the shape (print width and two-space indent) and typescript-eslint supplies the depth rules, among them no-else-return and switch-exhaustiveness-check for flat discriminant switches. The type system adds one twist: an early return that ends a discriminated-union function needs a never-typed call (or 'satisfies never') for the compiler to keep narrowing, so flat code and exhaustiveness checks are usually written together. Hand-formatting survives only in repositories with no formatter; there, keep the file's convention.
pitfalls: Prettier's printWidth (80 by default) wraps a long condition across lines whose continuation indent looks like a block; extract the predicate into a named boolean before that happens.

A plain throw at the end of a union-dispatching function does not narrow like a never-typed helper, so without assertNever the compiler stops flagging unhandled variants; typescript-eslint's switch-exhaustiveness-check only covers switches.
Decorator-heavy or framework-generated code keeps nesting inside lifecycle and template methods; the formatter fixes the shape but not the depth.
